en: A state that is neither skillful nor acquired by clinging and not subject to clinging is a condition, by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇa-paccaya*), for a state that is indeterminate, acquired by clinging, and subject to clinging...
[six questions] (abbreviated). Regarding the object-condition there are six; regarding the proximate, the immediate, and the decisive support conditions, there are six;

regarding the prenascence condition, three; regarding the kamma condition, five; regarding the nutriment condition, three; regarding the presence condition, three... pe ...regarding the non-disappearance condition, three.

Dependent on a state that is neither wholesome nor acquired through clinging but is subject to clinging, there arises an indeterminate state that is not acquired through clinging but is subject to clinging, by way of root-condition.

(Abbreviated. Under root-condition there are five; under predominance-condition there are five ... pe ... under result-condition there are three ... pe ... under non-disappearance-condition there are five.

Dependent on a state that is neither wholesome nor not acquired through clinging and not subject to clinging, there arises a wholesome state that is not acquired through clinging and not subject to clinging.

It arises by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated. Six with respect to the root, six with respect to the object … pe … three with respect to repetition … pe … three with respect to result … pe … six with respect to non-disappearance.
